newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan auto industry leads economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan auto industry leads economic recovery.

text.p: Venezuela's economic recovery, which is projected to grow more than five percent this year, is being led by a dramatic turnaround in the local automobile industry, industry officials said Monday.
"This is one of the first sectors to move with the economic recovery," Carlos Gonzalez, director of the Venezuelan Chamber of Vehicle Parts Manufacturers (Favenpa), told a news conference.
Sales of domestically assembled and imported vehicles jumped about 160 percent in the first half of 1997 and the trend is expected to continue.
"We are in a steady process of growth. We are expecting sales of 150,000 units this year and in 1998 about 170,000 units," Gonzalez said.
Sales in 1996 totaled about 70,000 units as the local economy contacted by 1.6 percent.
Exports were also growing with a 52 percent increase over the first six months to 10,107 units, compared to 6,641 units in the first half of 1996.
"We think that Venezuela can this year resume exporting finished vehicles to the Andean Community. We see exports surpassing 20,000 units (for 1997 as a whole)," Gonzalez said.

The growth in domestic vehicle sales had boosted employment in the sector by between 30 to 40 percent and would see auto part sales grow 40 percent to $875 million from $625 million last year, Favenpa said.
